Safety First! is a gleefully absurd physics-based puzzle game that turns a mundane concept—repairing electrical wiring—into a chaotic exercise in coordination, patience, and slapstick comedy. Developed by JCO and published by Headup, the game wears its silliness on its sleeve, presenting a deliberately clumsy control scheme and exaggerated physics as the foundation of both its challenge and its humor. What initially looks like a joke premise quickly reveals itself to be a tightly structured puzzle experience that thrives on failure just as much as success.

The central mechanic revolves around using a magical yellow repair liquid to reconnect broken power cables, but the true challenge lies in simply moving your character. Each leg is controlled independently, forcing players to think about balance, timing, and momentum in ways that feel awkward by design. Walking across a room, climbing a ladder, or standing still without collapsing can be more difficult than the puzzle objective itself. This deliberate lack of elegance transforms basic movement into a constant problem-solving exercise, where even minor actions require focus and experimentation. The result is a game that consistently produces unexpected outcomes, many of them hilarious, as your character stumbles, stretches, or accidentally dismantles themselves in the process.

Level progression is divided across multiple campaigns that gradually layer new constraints onto the same core idea. Early levels focus on teaching the fundamentals of movement and aiming the repair fluid, allowing players to acclimate to the unusual controls. Later stages introduce stricter rules, such as limiting how feet can be lifted or altering environmental physics, which forces players to rethink strategies they may have relied on earlier. A space-themed campaign adds zero gravity into the mix, turning movement into an entirely different challenge where inertia and drifting replace friction and footing. This escalation keeps the experience feeling fresh even though the core mechanic remains unchanged.

One of the game’s standout qualities is how it embraces variety through optional modes that dramatically change tone and behavior. Special modes alter music, movement speed, physics, and audio effects, transforming familiar levels into wildly different experiences. These modes are not merely visual novelties; they meaningfully affect gameplay, sometimes making levels easier through speed or harder through instability. This willingness to let chaos take center stage adds replay value and encourages players to revisit completed levels just to see how badly things can go wrong in new circumstances.

Visually and aurally, Safety First! commits fully to its comedic identity. Character models are intentionally crude and exaggerated, reinforcing the idea that elegance is neither expected nor desired. Animations stretch and snap in ways that emphasize the physics-driven nature of the game, while sound effects punctuate every misstep and mishap with comedic timing. The soundtrack shifts dynamically depending on the mode, reinforcing the absurdity and keeping the experience lighthearted even during repeated failures. Together, these elements ensure that frustration rarely has time to settle before it turns into laughter.

Despite its humor, the game is not careless in its design. Levels are compact and quick to restart, encouraging experimentation without severe penalty. Failure is frequent but rarely feels punishing, as each attempt provides immediate feedback and often reveals a new approach. However, the same qualities that define the game’s charm can also be barriers. The control scheme is intentionally unforgiving, and players who dislike physics-heavy movement or trial-and-error gameplay may find the experience more irritating than entertaining. The aesthetic and tone are also unapologetically niche, favoring crude comedy over broad appeal.

Ultimately, Safety First! succeeds by fully committing to its own ridiculous vision. It transforms frustration into humor and awkwardness into challenge, offering a puzzle game where mastery feels genuinely earned because nothing ever behaves quite the way you expect. It is not a game about precision in the traditional sense, but about adaptation, persistence, and learning to laugh at failure. For players who enjoy unconventional mechanics, physics-driven chaos, and games that value personality over polish, Safety First! delivers a memorable and surprisingly engaging experience that stands out in the indie puzzle landscape.

Rating: 7/10

[h2]Sinopsis[/h2]
Safety First es un divertido juego de puzzles basado en físicas. La premisa es sencilla, tendremos que aplicar "Líquido Mágico Amarillo Reparador" sobre cables rotos para arreglarlos, o lo que es lo mismo, orinar dentro de un enchufe. La dificultad de cada puzzle radica en el movimiento de cada pierna por separado, lo cual es más complicado de lo que parece, especialmente cuando los niveles empiezan a hacerse cada vez más complejos, así como los obstáculos a superar.

[h2]Jugabilidad / Apartado técnico[/h2]
La gracia está en el peculiar movimiento del personaje, si jugamos con mando cada stick controlará una pierna (con teclado podemos usar WASD y flechas), tendremos que ir desplazándonos cuidadosamente hasta conseguir direccionar nuestro aparato miccionador hacia el hueco objetivo y una vez apuntemos, disparar una bola de fluido amarillo. Si separamos demasiado las piernas podemos acabar desmembrados, debiendo empezar de cero. Los puzzles se harán cada vez más complejos con plataformas de distintos tamaños o en movimiento, situaciones donde debemos mantener el equilibrio en posiciones comprometidas o en los que debemos mover objetos para usarlos como plataformas o escaleras, las combinaciones son muy ingeniosas y abundantes. Tendremos que lidiar con 3 campañas, "Clásica", "Avanzada", donde solo podremos levantar un pie a la vez y "Espacial", donde tendremos que lidiar con puzzles en gravedad cero. Además, si nos sabe a poco, dispondremos de otros modos de juego con ciertos handicaps, en el modo PEP todo va mucho más rápido y en el modo DRNK jugaremos como si fuésemos borrachos mientras gritamos improperios en alemán.

[h2]Valoración[/h2]
Me ha parecido un juego extremadamente divertido e ingenioso, tanto por su concepto surrealista, como por sus mecánicas originales y bastante complicadas a veces. Ojo, algunos niveles pueden ser desesperantes, ya que exigen una precisión bastante elevada. Si te gustan los puzzles, los retos y el humor absurdo, dale un tiento, es un buen juego. El juego me ha llevado unas 10 horas y media completarlo al 100%. Funciona en Steam Deck, aunque me ha dado algunos problemas en esta plataforma para conseguir los logros.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

"Safety First!" ist ein albernes 2D Twin-Stick Physik-basiertes Spielchen.

Wobei man Physik unbedingt definieren sollte. "Safety First!" steht in der Tradition von Fun-Spielchen wie "Goat Simulator" "I am Bread", wir bewegen uns hier allerdings nur in einer 2D-Welt. Mit dem Gamepad versuchen wir eine extrem sensibel reagierende Spielfigur zu kontrollieren und haben dabei zahlreiche zu beachtende Eingabemöglichkeiten. 

Mit den Sticks kontrollieren wir die Beine oder genauer gesagt die Füße der Spielfigur, die aus zahlreichen sehr schwabbelig agierende Elementen besteht. So müssen wir schon allein bei kleinen Bewegungen damit rechnen, daß es unsere Figur aufgrund der Eigenbewegung der Extremitäten zerreißt und wir allein dadurch schon das jeweilige Level verlieren. 

Und die Aufgabe? In kleine Vertiefungen müssen wir unsere nur begrenzt vorhandene magische gelbe Reparier-Flüssigkeit spritzen, die sich aus einem kleinen Strich unterhalb unserer Unterleibs ergießt. Anders gesagt: Zielpissen. 

Das trifft dann anscheinend das Fäkal-Humorzentrum Vieler, die sich selbst wohl als Junggeblieben bezeichnen würden. Ich finde den diese Komikebene eher bemüht und angestrengt, vor allem da sie völlig kontextungebunden daherkommt.

Allerdings muß man dem Spiel zumindest zugute halten, daß es recht kreativ mit dem Leveldesign agiert, gute Ideen hat und immer wieder für Abwechslung sorgt, auch wenn das Schaffen eines Levels weitaus mehr mit Glück als mit kontrollierbarer Kontrolle zu tun hat. 

Auch ästhetisch ist das Game stilsicher ohne allerdings wirklich kreativ zu sein. Einfachheit und Reduktion sind hier Thema, was allerdings auch durchaus zum Genre paßt. Sogar Musik und Sound sind recht nett.

Wer das Genre mag, findet einen qualitativ guten Vertreter.

It's not what I would really call a game; it's more an interactive manual on electrical engineering and how to avoid safety hazards while working on projects. It's actually been a tremendous help to me in my daily life, because as someone with little real-world skills, it taught me how to change a fuse or fix a frayed, dangerous wire.

In short, it's not a particulary fun game, but it certainly is a helpful one. Couldn't recommend more.
